quotes.text: Grant and receive scoped payment credentials for agent-initiated purchases.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Shared payment tokens (SPTs) are available to agents, customers, and sellers in the US.

An SPT is a scoped grant to use the customer’s payment method. The agent grants SPTs to your [Stripe profile](https://docs.stripe.com/get-started/account/profile.md), each with usage and expiration limits.
After you receive a granted `SharedPaymentToken`, create a `PaymentIntent` to complete the payment.
After the customer completes the required action, Stripe sends the `shared_payment.issued_token.active` webhook unless you deactivated the `SharedPaymentToken` in the meantime.
To test your integration in live mode, use the [link-cli](https://link.com/agents) to issue SPTs from your personal Link account.
You receive this event when the seller uses the SPT.

findings: The same base URL produced a full 431-line seller and agent guide on 2026-05-12 (old lines 1-431), but the 2026-11-07 capture is a 15-line index whose only detailed routes are Sellers, Agents, and Connect platforms variants (new lines 1-15). This is a capture/rendering scope change, not evidence that SPT functionality was removed.

The new index establishes only the general scoped-payment-credential purpose and three variant navigation URLs (new lines 7, 11-15). It does not restate the old guide's US availability, seller and agent prerequisites, API calls, payment-method support, usage limits, authentication states, or webhooks (old lines 8-431).

The existing mapped source is explicitly dated 2026-05-12 and its raw_files points to the full May guide (source lines 1-8, 11-53). The Stripe index and shared-payment-tokens concept route to that source. The November index should not replace its factual raw evidence or be added to raw_files as if it supported detailed seller and agent claims.

The May guide has only seller and agent bodies; the November index adds a Connect platforms navigation variant (new line 15). Its contents were not captured in this job and cannot be inferred from the label.

Narrow source correction needed: the current source's single 'Test' line treats testHelpers and Link CLI spend-request as interchangeable (source line 23). The May guide distinguishes test-mode simulation with testHelpers (old lines 23-25) from a live-mode Link CLI one-time spend request requiring Link login/payment method and --request-approval (old lines 52-77). Recommend separate labeled test-helper and live-mode Link CLI lines so a test-only query cannot select a live spend request.

Narrow concept correction needed: the concept says 'US only' in unqualified present tense and lists methods as current support (concept lines 10, 56), whereas these are May-capture statements (old lines 8, 329-340). Recommend date-stamping both to the 2026-05-12 guide and retaining the buyer-controlled Affirm loan-application UI and marketing qualifications; the November variant index establishes no current geography or method eligibility (new lines 5-15).

Narrow concept correction needed: the concept's 'used' webhook row says 'Seller charged the SPT' (concept line 64), but the May guide says the event fires when the seller uses the SPT (old line 430). Recommend 'seller used the SPT' and a separate payment-outcome check; neither token use nor activation proves a succeeded or settled PaymentIntent (old lines 82-100, 428-431).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the 2026-05-12 US availability and supported-method statements explicitly dated to the full guide; absence from the November index is not a region or eligibility change (old lines 8, 329-340; new lines 5-15).

Keep separate seller granted-token and agent issued-token roles, seller Stripe profile and agent profile collection, and scoped usage/expiration limits as May guide claims (old lines 14-25, 145-160, 302-325).
Keep the May guide's public-preview SDK examples qualified as examples, not proof of current SDK or merchant eligibility (old lines 27-42, 84-98, 308-327).

Keep the requires_action, active, used, and deactivated lifecycle distinctions and the need to handle customer 3DS/redirect actions; active means the token can continue through payment, and used means seller used the token, neither being proof of a succeeded or settled payment (old lines 342-404, 419-431).
Keep the May guide's limited Affirm conditions and buyer-controlled loan application UI, rather than broadening the supported-method table (old lines 329-340).
conflicts: Retained source line 23 conflates testHelpers simulation with the separately labeled live-mode Link CLI flow in old lines 23-25 and 52-77; correct the source wording without treating the November omission as a behavior change.

Retained concept lines 10 and 56 present May 2026 US scope and supported methods as current; date those claims and retain old line 340's Affirm buyer-controlled UI limits because new lines 5-15 provide no updated eligibility evidence.

Retained concept line 64 equates issued-token used with charging; old line 430 describes token use, while old lines 82-100 and 428-431 do not establish final PaymentIntent success. Correct the row and keep payment outcome separate.
unresolved_questions: The seller, agent, and Connect variant bodies were not among the four pinned files; this job cannot establish their November wording, current feature support, US scope, preview status, or Connect-specific flow.
The base URL index alone cannot confirm any account's SPT access, live payment execution, authentication completion, or final settlement.
